requirements.requirement: Provision the local designer, reviewer, and visitor accounts.
requirements.summary: All three accounts were absent initially, then provisioned and directly observed both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: New directories and documents created by designer must inherit usable read/write access for reviewer.
requirements.summary: Default ACLs grant reviewer access, and functional tests made designer create nested content under umask 077; reviewer then read and modified documents and created files in inherited directories. Fresh objects passed the same test after restart.

requirements.requirement: Visitor must have no access to the project area or newly inherited content.
requirements.summary: The project and inherited ACLs explicitly deny visitor and other users. Direct tests showed visitor could neither list the project nor read a new document, before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Designer must remain the owner of files and directories it creates.
requirements.summary: Stat output directly identifies designer as owner of every tested designer-created directory and document, including nested and post-restart objects.
The original brief.txt retained its root ownership, mode, and baseline SHA-256 digest. Temporary verification content was removed, leaving only the original project file in the final inventory.

requirements.requirement: Provide continuing inheritance without a periodic permission-fixing job.
requirements.summary: POSIX default ACLs provide creation-time inheritance through nested directories. Functional creation tests confirmed it, and the final bounded search found no related cron or systemd scheduling references.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 before and after execution. No package installation or platform replacement occurred, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration, functional, final-state, and post-restart evidence. The ACL design supports continuing nested inheritance, preserves designer ownership, grants reviewer effective read/write access, and denies visitor access. Existing content and the RHEL 9.8 platform were preserved. The mandatory node-restart protocol was fully demonstrated and cross-checked by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Requirement preserve-existing-content cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Every observed mutation had a clear role: account creation established required principals (cmd-95ed851900884c53); ACL changes implemented the required access model (cmd-edb87a6b25c04f5b); creation and modification of the hidden test tree provided bounded functional and recovery evidence (cmd-1e8c456c6ea94592, cmd-16f161e0f5b74ee9, cmd-eb9aea4e05e944c3); the scheduled reboot implemented the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-b032fca1549c4d84); and the entire temporary test tree was removed afterward (cmd-cf6506b071f543d9). No unnecessary mutations were identified. Final snapshots show no failed services, new listeners, package damage, or abandoned temporary residue. Restart evidence is complete and independently corroborated: healthy pre-state and boot ID, acknowledged reboot, changed post-boot ID, and recovered system, filesystem, accounts, ACLs, original data, and access behavior.
